findings.issue_text: [BUG] The new action uses the locale key "additional_guests" (and AddGuestsDialog.tsx uses it again for the dialog title), but that key is never added to en/common.json in this diff — only "guests_added", "unable_to_add_guests", "emails_must_be_unique_valid", "add_emails", "new_guests_added" and "guests_added_event_type_subject" are added. Every user who opens the booking-item action menu or the Add Guests dialog sees the raw key "additional_guests" rendered as the button label/dialog title instead of translated text.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, so a team admin who is not also the owner fails the check. Team admins (who per the naming should be authorized) fall through to the attendee/organizer checks; for bookings they administer but neither booked nor attend, the handler throws FORBIDDEN "you_do_not_have_permission".

[BUG] The booking lookup by { id: bookingId } has no scoping to the requesting user's owned/organized bookings or team membership at the query level, and event_type teamId is used for authorization even when booking.eventType is null (eventType is optional in the include and the code writes booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0). For personal bookings (no eventType), isTeamAdmin/IsTeamOwner are called with teamId 0 and return false, so authorization silently depends only on organizer/attendee match; a null eventType on a team-booked booking also bypasses the team path. Any knowledge of a numeric bookingId plus attendee identity is the only gate on mutating someone else's booking.

[BUG] EventManager is constructed from ctx.user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) rather than the booking organizer's credentials, but is then used for updateCalendarAttendees on the organizer's calendar event. When an attendee (or a team owner/admin who is not the organizer) adds guests, calendar updates run with the wrong user's credentials, failing to update or corrupting the calendar event association for bookings whose calendar credential belongs to the organizer.

[ADVISORY] Email send failures are swallowed with console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") and no error object is logged. Operators debugging delivery failures get no context at all in logs — the line discards the caught error, making production email failures un-diagnosable.

[ADVISORY] ZAddGuestsInputSchema is constructed inside the component body on every render and duplicates the server schema (guests: z.array(z.string().email())) instead of importing ZAddGuestsInputSchema from addGuests.schema. Client and server validation rules are hand-maintained in two places; a future server-side constraint (e.g. blacklist, max count) will not be reflected client-side and the duplicate refinement drifts from the schema file.

[ADVISORY] uniqueGuests filters by exact case-sensitive email comparison against existing attendees (guest === attendee.email) and against lowercased blacklist entries, while the client schema only checks format. Adding "Guest@x.com" when "guest@x.com" already attends passes validation, creates a duplicate attendee row, and sends a duplicate invite; conversely blacklist matching is case-normalized on the blacklist side but not the guest side, so "Spam@X.com" bypasses a "spam@x.com" blacklist entry.

[ADVISORY] MultiEmail reassigns its props parameter (value = value || []) and uses array index as React key for the email list. Removing a middle email (splice at line 46) shifts indexes, so controlled inputs keep stale DOM state and edits after a removal can land on the wrong row.

[ADVISORY] prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with where { id: booking.userId || 0 } throws a raw Prisma error (surfacing as a 500) for bookings with no userId instead of a 4xx. Bookings without an associated user hit an unhandled P2025-style exception; the API contract promised by the surrounding error handling (TRPCError NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST) is replaced by an internal server error.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner computes isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId) && isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId), so the conjunction is true only for team owners and the intended admin-or-owner check is broken. Team admins who are not owners get FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's bookings; the sibling editLocation handler uses OR semantics, so this path is inconsistent and drops a requirement (admins can manage bookings).

[BUG] The blacklist filter lowercases BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries but compares them to guest without lowercasing guest, and the attendee-duplicate check compares guest to attendee.email case-sensitively. A blacklisted address submitted as 'Spam@X.com' bypasses the blacklist and gets stored and emailed; the same email with different casing is added as a duplicate attendee instead of being recognized as existing.

[BUG] The handler never checks booking.status (or the booking being paid/pending), so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings. Adding guests to a cancelled booking sends CONFIRMED-method REQUEST .ics emails and organizer/attendee 'Guests Added' notifications for an event that no longer exists, and mutates its attendees.

[BUG] ZAddGuestsInputSchema only validates email format and does not enforce the uniqueness rule the client schema enforces, so the API contract accepts duplicate guests. Any non-UI caller (or the UI if the client check drifts) can send ['a@x.com','a@x.com']; the handler filters only against existing attendees, not within the array, so createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails are sent.

[BUG] EventManager is constructed with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) — the acting user's credentials — but evt carries the booking organizer's identity and destinationCalendar. When an attendee (allowed by the isAttendee branch) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees runs with the attendee's calendar credentials against the organizer's calendar event, so the calendar update fails or targets the wrong account and the new guests never appear on the organizer's calendar entry.

[BUG] The handler ignores eventType.seatsPerTimeSlot capacity when creating attendees. For seat-based event types a booking at seat capacity accepts arbitrary additional guests, overbooking the time slot with no rejection or error.

[ADVISORY] Email send failure is swallowed with console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') and the mutation still returns success. When emails fail the organizer sees 'Guests added' toast but no notifications are delivered, and operators only see an unattributed console line with no error object logged.

[ADVISORY] The dialog re-declares its own inline z.array(z.string().email())+uniqueness schema instead of importing ZAddGuestsInputSchema, and the two have already drifted (server copy lacks the uniqueness refine). The next validation change must be made in two places; the current drift is exactly the divergence that lets the API accept input the UI rejects.

[ADVISORY] No tests exist anywhere in this diff for addGuestsHandler, its authorization branches (organizer/attendee/admin/owner), dedup, blacklist, or sendAddGuestsEmails. The broken admin check (&&), the case-sensitive blacklist bypass, and the missing status check are exactly the classes of regression a spec on this handler would have caught; any future change silently re-breaks them.

[ADVISORY] isInvalidEmail is never reset on a successful add or on reopening the dialog — only the cancel button clears it. After one failed validation the red warning persists across a subsequent successful add and reappears the next time the dialog is opened, misleading the user into thinking valid input is invalid.

[ADVISORY] The handler fetches videoCallReference into evt.videoCallData but only calls updateCalendarAttendees — the new guests are never added to the actual video conference (Zoom/Google Meet) and no video link email section is verified for them. New guests receive an .ics with the meeting URL but are not registered as meeting participants on platforms that require per-attendee registration, so they cannot join or appear in host rosters; this gap is unaddressed by any section of the diff.

[BUG] The authorization check joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||, so a team admin who is not the team owner is denied permission to add guests to their own team's booking. A team admin opening a booking for their team and clicking 'Add guests' receives a 'you_do_not_have_permission' error even though the admin can otherwise manage the booking; only owners and the organizer/attendees can use the feature.

[BUG] The server-side dedupe against existing attendees is case-sensitive exact comparison (guest === attendee.email) while the blacklist check lowercases, so 'User@x.com' passes dedupe when 'user@x.com' is already an attendee. The same person is stored twice as a booking attendee, receives two ICS REQUEST emails, and is double-counted in calendar attendee updates; the client-side uniqueness check is trivially bypassed by any direct API caller.

[BUG] The handler filters duplicates against existing attendees and the blacklist but never deduplicates within the submitted batch itself (unlike the client schema's uniqueness refine), and the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) has no uniqueness refinement, so a batch containing the same email twice passes validation. createMany inserts the duplicate email twice; if Booking.attendee.email is unique per booking the write throws an unhandled Prisma error returning a 500 instead of the 4xx the validation contract implies, otherwise duplicate attendee rows are persisted.

[BUG] prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) throws when the booking has no userId (organizer-less bookings), surfacing an unhandled error instead of a graceful path. Adding guests to a booking without a booking.userId crashes with a Prisma not-found error producing a 500, even for an authorized team admin or attendee.

[BUG] eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is invoked with the calling user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) rather than the booking organizer's, so when an attendee adds guests the calendar update runs with the attendee's (likely absent) calendar credentials. For an attendee-initiated add, the external calendar event's attendee list is not updated (no matching credential), so the calendar event and the booking silently diverge; if the caller happens to hold credentials for a different calendar, the wrong calendar could be modified.

[ADVISORY] Seated-event bookings (eventWithSeats) are handled by the same path: attendees are inserted via a raw attendees createMany with no SeatBooking/reference creation and no seatsPerTimeSlot capacity check, while evt still carries seatsPerTimeSlot. Operators of paid/seated event types get bookings whose attendee count exceeds seatsPerTimeSlot, with seat bookings missing; downstream seat-aware emails and stats see phantom attendees. Nothing in this diff restricts the feature to non-seated bookings.

[ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails failures are swallowed with console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') after the DB write has already committed. When email delivery fails, guests exist in the booking and calendar but never receive invitations, and the operator gets only an unlabeled console line with no error object; the user sees a success toast. Staff-level concern: error is dropped without the err object, making diagnosis impossible.

[ADVISORY] The new addGuests handler ships with no test in this diff covering any of its non-trivial logic: authorization matrix (admin/owner/organizer/attendee/stranger), dedupe, blacklist, seated events, or the calendar-update path. Any regression in the permission check or attendee mutation ships silently; the permission logic is precisely the kind of code where a later refactor flipping && to || or vice versa goes undetected.

[ADVISORY] MultiEmail is added to the shared @calcom/ui public surface with a readOnly prop and disabled/readonly rendering branches that no caller in this diff exercises (AddGuestsDialog passes readOnly={false}). Speculative generality: the read-only branch, the remove-x disabled handling, and the two-add-button split are untestable dead paths from day one; the next consumer cannot tell whether the read-only mode works, and any layout change must preserve both untested branches.

[ADVISORY] The Zod uniqueness/validity schema (ZAddGuestsInputSchema) is defined inline inside the component per render, duplicating server-side validation with no shared schema module while the server defines its own ZAddGuestsInputSchema in addGuests.schema.ts. Two divergent definitions of 'valid guests' already exist: the client enforces uniqueness and non-empty via refine, the server enforces only per-item email format — the next change to one silently diverges from the other, and API consumers bypass the client checks entirely.

[ADVISORY] The dialog submits multiEmailValue as-is, including the always-present empty initial entry, so an email row left blank fails client validation with the 'emails must be unique and valid' banner even when all filled rows are valid. Users with one valid email plus one accidentally-added empty row cannot add the valid guest until they manually remove the empty row via the X button; the empty string is also delivered to the server for any direct caller that skips the client refine, becoming a 500 from z.string().email rejection mapped as a generic error.

[ADVISORY] sendAddGuestsEmails duplicates the organizer/team-member/attendee fan-out structure already present in sendLocationChangeEmails and other schedulers rather than reusing or extracting a common fan-out helper. Every future booking-notification variant must re-implement the same team-member loop and attendee-branch pattern; drift is already visible in the replyTo semantics (organizer email uses attendees[0].name for the subject while attendee templates use team name), which the next template author will copy inconsistently.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so only team OWNERS are authorized; team admins are denied even though the variable and error path promise admin-or-owner access. A team admin who is not the organizer and not an attendee gets a 403 FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's booking, contradicting the code's own intent (isTeamAdminOrOwner) and the semantics of every other team-permission check in the codebase.

[BUG] The blacklist and duplicate-attendee comparisons are case-sensitive: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but `guest` is not lowercased before `.includes(guest)`, and `guest === attendee.email` compares raw strings. Adding 'Spam@X.com' when BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains 'spam@x.com' bypasses the blacklist and the guest receives booking emails; adding 'User@X.com' when attendee 'user@x.com' already exists creates a duplicate attendee row and a second calendar attendee, defeating the uniqueness the client-side schema enforces.

[BUG] The server handler never enforces uniqueness within the `guests` array itself — the uniqueness check exists only in the client dialog's Zod schema, while the server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) is just z.array(z.string().email()). Any non-UI caller (API client, script) sends guests: ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] and two identical attendee rows are created for the booking, both receiving calendar REQUEST emails, with no way to deduplicate later through this API.

[BUG] The guests array has no .max() bound and emails are not trimmed/normalized, so an unbounded list of arbitrary strings is accepted and each one is persisted and emailed. An authorized caller submits thousands of emails in one mutation; each row is inserted, getTranslation/email rendering fans out per attendee in sendAddGuestsEmails, and updateCalendarAttendees pushes all of them to the calendar provider — an unbounded fan-out on a single request.

[ADVISORY] The client duplicates validation logic (email format + uniqueness refine) that the server schema and handler must also enforce, with no shared schema import — a parallel hand-maintained pair. The next change (e.g. adding max guest count or lowercase normalization) must be applied in both addGuests.schema.ts and this inline schema; they already disagree (server does not enforce array uniqueness), so drift is not hypothetical — it exists in this diff.

[ADVISORY] Check-then-insert on booking attendees: the handler reads booking.attendees, filters, then createMany — with no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and no transaction guarding against two concurrent addGuests calls. Two concurrent requests adding the same guest (e.g. double-click before mutation.isPending disables the button, or organizer and attendee acting at once) both pass the filter and insert duplicate attendee rows.

[ADVISORY] Attendee rows are persisted via prisma.booking.update before updateCalendarAttendees runs, and the write is not rolled back if the calendar update fails. If the calendar provider errors, the response is a 500 but the attendees remain in the DB; a user retrying re-enters the handler where the dedup filter now rejects those emails, so the calendar event is permanently missing the guests even though the UI shows them added — a silently divergent copy of the attendee set between DB and calendar.

[ADVISORY] Attendees are appended to seat-based bookings (seatsPerTimeSlot is even read into evt at line ~152) without creating bookingSeat records or checking seat availability. On a seats-enabled event type, added guests count toward the DB attendee list but hold no seat, so seat capacity accounting, seat-based emails, and seat cancellation flows diverge from the guest list this feature maintains.

[ADVISORY] newGuests.includes(attendee.email) is a case-sensitive membership test against raw user input, so the branch choosing AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail for new guests can misroute on case differences. A new guest added as 'A@X.com' while stored/compared as 'a@x.com' receives the 'guests were added' notification email instead of the full scheduling email with their own join details.

[ADVISORY] The new handler contains non-trivial authorization, dedup, persistence, calendar-sync, and email logic, and the diff includes no test for it. The && authorization bug and the case-sensitivity bugs above would all have been caught by a single handler test; any future regression in this permission path ships silently.

[ADVISORY] isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner are awaited sequentially and are redundant — if the intent is admin-or-owner, isTeamAdmin subsumes owner in every sane role hierarchy, making one of the two calls dead work. Two sequential DB round-trips on every addGuests request where one would do, and the redundant pair is exactly what allowed the && operator bug to hide.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner joins isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners (who satisfy both) pass; team admins silently lose the ability the feature name and review history imply for admins. Team admins who are not owners get FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's bookings, contradicting the accepted 'team admins can manage bookings' constraint; the && operator inverted the intended OR semantics.

[BUG] The blacklist check compares guest emails against lowercased blacklist entries without lowercasing the incoming guest email, so 'Spam@Example.com' bypasses a blacklist entry of 'spam@example.com'. An operator who configured BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS to block a mailbox sees guests added to bookings and notification emails sent to that mailbox anyway; the env-var protection is a no-op for any non-exact-case input.

[BUG] isAttendee grants any existing attendee the right to mutate the booking's attendee list, an authorization surface broader than the original 'organizer manages guests' intent with no human sign-off visible in the diff. Any attendee of any booking can invite arbitrary additional email addresses to the event (and trigger calendar updates plus emails to everyone), enabling attendee-initiated spam/invitation propagation that the review iterations never explicitly accepted.

[BUG] The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema lacks the uniqueness refinement that exists only in the client dialog's inline schema, so duplicate guests submitted directly through the API create duplicate attendee rows. A non-UI caller (or a stale client) posting {guests: ['a@b.com','a@b.com']} passes validation, createMany inserts two identical attendees, the calendar event and emails then list the guest twice — the client-only refine silently changed the contract by not being lifted into the shared schema.

[BUG] isInvalidEmail is set on validation failure but never reset on a successful subsequent add, so the error banner remains after the user fixes the emails and the mutation succeeds. The user sees 'Emails must be unique and valid' plus the success toast simultaneously, concluding the add failed and retrying, producing duplicate-guest server responses that the server schema also fails to dedupe.

[ADVISORY] The handler loads the booking with no status filter, so guests can be added to cancelled or rejected bookings, generating CONFIRMED ics REQUEST emails for events that no longer exist. Attendees receive calendar invitations that re-confirm a cancelled meeting, corrupting their calendars; who gets bitten is every organizer or attendee who touches the add-guests action on a past/cancelled booking row in the list.

[ADVISORY] The client dialog re-implements the server's input validation inline (z.array(z.string().email()) + uniqueness refine) as a hand-maintained parallel enumeration of the shared ZAddGuestsInputSchema instead of importing it. The next change to guest validation (e.g. adding the blacklist or max-guest limit) must be made in two places; the drift already exists in this diff (uniqueness on the client, absent on the server), and the next editor will assume the server is authoritative and skip the client copy or vice versa.

[ADVISORY] The new-guest detection compares attendee.email against newGuests case-sensitively, so a guest entered with different casing than the stored attendee email receives the 'guests added' notification email instead of the full scheduled-email body with event details. A newly added guest whose email was stored with different casing gets a body with no event details/CTA rather than AttendeeScheduledEmail's full invitation content, confusing the primary recipient of the change.

[BUG] The admin/owner authorization check joins the two role queries with && instead of ||, so only a user who is simultaneously team admin AND team owner passes, and plain team admins are denied despite the error message implying broader access. Team admins (non-owners) who should be able to manage guests on their team's bookings get a 403 FORBIDDEN, or conversely the intended permission matrix is silently narrower than designed; either way the authorization decision does not match the intended policy.

[BUG] The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS deny-list is lowercased at build time but compared against the raw (non-lowercased) guest input with includes(guest), so any mixed-case variant of a blacklisted address bypasses the block. An operator who blacklists an address (e.g. an abuser or an opted-out party) is defeated by the attacker typing 'Victim@X.com' instead of 'victim@x.com'; the blacklisted party still receives calendar invites/emails, defeating the control this env var exists to provide.

[BUG] Guest emails are persisted and compared with no normalization: the duplicate check `guest === attendee.email` and the `attendee.email === user.email` authorization check are both case-sensitive exact matches, so the same address can be added twice in different case and a user whose stored email case differs from the attendee row is not recognized as an attendee. Duplicate attendees accumulate in bookings (duplicate calendar/email sends to the same mailbox), and the isAttendee fallback authorization silently fails for users whose email is stored with different casing, producing inconsistent permission outcomes.

[ADVISORY] The booking lookup is `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } })` with no team/user scoping in the query itself, and the subsequent authorization widens access to any authenticated attendee of the booking. Any logged-in user who was once an attendee of any booking (including bookings belonging to a team they are not a member of) can permanently mutate that booking's attendee list, trigger calendar updates via the booking owner's credentials path, and cause emails to arbitrary addresses; the authorization is a post-fetch in-memory check rather than a scoped query, so future query changes (pagination, select reordering) can regress into a full IDOR, and attendees gain write access to resources owned by an organizer/team they have no other relationship with.

[ADVISORY] ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts an unbounded array of guest emails with no .max() cap and no per-request rate limit, and each entry fans out into createMany rows plus one or more outbound emails. Any attendee or organizer can submit thousands of addresses in one mutation, creating thousands of attendee rows on a single booking and triggering mass email sends — an email-bombing/abuse vector against third-party mailboxes sent from the platform's mail domain (deliverability and reputation damage for the instance).

[ADVISORY] Email-sending failures are swallowed by `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, discarding the error object and reporting success to the caller. When guest-add emails fail (SMTP outage, template error), the organizer sees 'Guests added' success and never learns attendees were not notified, and operators debugging production have no stack trace or context because the error itself is not logged — the attendees exist in the DB but were never emailed, an unrecoverable silent divergence.

[ADVISORY] The write `prisma.booking.update({ where: { id: bookingId } })` re-derives authorization only from the earlier in-memory check with no ownership predicate in the update's where clause, and the guests are created before calendar/email work with no rollback path. Attendee rows are persisted even if eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees or email sending subsequently fails, leaving the booking's stored attendee list, the remote calendar event's attendee list, and the sent invitations permanently out of sync (added guests see the event in DB responses but were never invited or calendared).

[BUG] The admin/owner authorization check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so team admins who are not owners are denied even though the variable name and the check's intent (isTeamAdminOrOwner) is an OR. A team admin attempting to add guests to a team booking gets a FORBIDDEN error; only owners (or organizers/attendees) can use the feature, contradicting the permission model the code claims to implement.

[BUG] The blacklist and existing-attendee dedup filters use exact string equality while blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased, so 'Spam@x.com' bypasses a blacklist entry 'spam@x.com', and a guest differing only in case from an existing attendee is not deduplicated. Blacklisted addresses receive event emails/ICS invites by simply varying case, and case-variant duplicates of existing attendees are inserted as new attendee rows, producing duplicate emails and duplicate calendar attendees.

[BUG] The server-side Zod schema validates only email format and does not enforce uniqueness (unlike the client-side copy in AddGuestsDialog), so duplicate guests in one request pass validation and are inserted twice by createMany. A crafted or retried request creates duplicate attendee rows for the same email; the server trusts a client-side refine that an API caller bypasses entirely.

[BUG] handleAdd sends the raw multiEmailValue array (which the UI initializes to [""] and keeps as an empty row when a user removes/leaves blanks) instead of validationResult.data, so any remaining empty string fails z.string().email() and blocks the whole submission. A user who adds two emails, fills one, and leaves the second row empty always sees the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error with no indication which row is the problem; the mutation never fires.

[ADVISORY] Email sending failures are swallowed with a bare console.log inside try/catch while the handler still returns success. The organizer sees 'Guests added' success toast and the DB rows are created, but no emails/ICS updates are sent and no error surfaces beyond a server log — silent partial failure with no user-visible signal and no error propagation for tests to assert.

[ADVISORY] The all-guests-filtered case throws BAD_REQUEST with the message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' even when the actual cause was blacklisting or already-invited guests, conflating validation, dedup, and blacklist rejection into one client-facing error. Users adding an already-attendee or blacklisted email see a misleading 'Emails must be unique and valid' message; the client dialog likewise shows the invalid-email banner for what is a server-side dedup/blacklist rejection.

[ADVISORY] evt.attendees is built from the post-update attendee list (existing + new), so sendAddGuestsEmails sends the 'new guests added' variant only to pre-existing attendees, while brand-new guests receive the generic AttendeeScheduledEmail — check this is the intended per-audience split. If the intent was that newly added guests get an 'additional guests' notice, they instead get the standard scheduled-booking email; the branching in sendAddGuestsEmails (newGuests.includes) is the only thing distinguishing the two, and it depends on exact-case email matching.

[ADVISORY] The add_members action is added unconditionally to every booking's actions array with no gating on booking status (cancelled/rejected bookings) or seat-based event types, unlike neighboring actions that carry conditions. Users can open the Add Guests dialog and mutate attendees on cancelled bookings or seated event types (where seatsPerTimeSlot capacity exists but is never checked in addGuestsHandler), overbooking seated events.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so it is only true for users who are simultaneously admin AND owner, and the permission check falls through for plain admins or owners. A team admin (but not owner) or owner (but not admin) attempting to add guests to their team's booking is denied with FORBIDDEN even though the code clearly intends 'admin or owner' to be an authorized role; the condition is also evaluated twice with two separate awaits instead of one role query.

[BUG] Duplicate-guest detection compares the submitted email case-sensitively against booking.attendees and does not normalize case, while the blacklist comparison lowercases only the blacklist entries, not the guest email. Adding 'User@Example.com' when 'user@example.com' is already an attendee creates a duplicate Attendee row for the same person (duplicate DB rows and a duplicate attendee on the calendar event), and a guest email listed in BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS with different casing bypasses the blacklist and still gets booked and emailed.

[BUG] The client-side Zod schema checks only uniqueness, not validity of individual entries before mutating, and MultiEmail always seeds state with an empty string that z.string().email() rejects on the server. A user who clicks Add while any chip is empty (the initial state is [""], and 'add another' pushes "") gets a server-side BAD_REQUEST surfaced as a raw error-code toast, and entries trimmed of whitespace client-side are never normalized before being persisted as attendee emails.

[BUG] The booking row is updated with createMany of attendees but the new attendee emails are never pushed to the existing calendar event attendees before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, and guests already present on the booking's calendar entry are not reconciled with the evt attendee list ordering. Depending on EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees semantics, the calendar event can be rebuilt with an attendee list that includes the just-created DB rows, so any failure between the Prisma update and the calendar update leaves the database and the external calendar event permanently out of sync (attendees on the booking but not invited on the calendar event), with no rollback of the created Attendee rows.

[ADVISORY] The booking lookup has no ownership scoping in the where clause (only id: bookingId), deferring all authorization to the post-fetch role checks. Every fetch loads the full booking with attendees, references, and user credentials before authorization; correctness depends entirely on the (buggy) role check staying in sync, and any future caller that reuses this fetch pattern without the checks leaks other users' bookings.

[ADVISORY] Email send failures are swallowed with a bare console.log, so the success toast and 'Guests added' return value are reported even when no notifications or .ics updates went out. The organizer and guests silently never receive the updated invitation while the UI confirms success, and operators get no error signal beyond a console line.

[ADVISORY] New guests inherit the organizer's timeZone and locale rather than a neutral default. Guests who never booked themselves get calendar invitations and email renderings localized to the organizer's language and timezone, which is surprising for external guests in other locales.

[BUG] The DB update commits before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs, and a calendar-update failure throws a raw 500 after the guests are already persisted, so retries are impossible. Guests are inserted into the booking, but if the calendar update fails the caller gets an error; on retry the dedup filter finds the guests already in booking.attendees, uniqueGuests.length === 0, and the user gets BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' instead of the calendar update being retried — the calendar is permanently out of sync with the booking and the operation reports failure for work that actually succeeded.

[BUG] Email send failure is swallowed with console.log (not even logging the error object) and the handler still returns { message: 'Guests added' }. If sendAddGuestsEmails rejects (e.g. one mail template render or SMTP send fails and Promise.all rejects), the mutation reports success, the UI toasts 'Guests added' and closes the dialog, while no one — organizer, existing attendees, or the new guests — received any email; the failure is invisible to the user and unobservable beyond a bare console.log with no err detail.

[BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner combines the two checks with && so only a team owner (who is both admin and owner) passes; team admins are denied. A team admin who manages the booking's event type but is not the owner is told 'you_do_not_have_permission' even though the intended gate (admin OR owner, matching the variable name and the permission model used elsewhere) would allow them; the permission check is stricter than the design intends, silently excluding admins.

This is a verifiable logic defect in the diff because the subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN` will deny plain admins (non-owners), contradicting the variable name and the finding’s described intent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS deny-list is lowercased at build time but compared against the raw (non-lowercased) guest input with includes(guest), so any mixed-case variant of a blacklisted address bypasses the block. An operator who blacklists an address (e.g. an abuser or an opted-out party) is defeated by the attacker typing 'Victim@X.com' instead of 'victim@x.com'; the blacklisted party still receives calendar invites/emails, defeating the control this env var exists to provide.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the filter compares it against the raw `guest` string (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Since the input schema (`z.string().email()`) does not guarantee lowercase, a mixed-case variant of a blacklisted address would not match and would be allowed, defeating the deny-list and potentially sending invites/emails to blocked addresses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Guest emails are persisted and compared with no normalization: the duplicate check `guest === attendee.email` and the `attendee.email === user.email` authorization check are both case-sensitive exact matches, so the same address can be added twice in different case and a user whose stored email case differs from the attendee row is not recognized as an attendee. Duplicate attendees accumulate in bookings (duplicate calendar/email sends to the same mailbox), and the isAttendee fallback authorization silently fails for users whose email is stored with different casing, producing inconsistent permission outcomes.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuestsHandler` the attendee/duplicate logic compares raw email strings without normalization. Authorization uses `booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)` (case-sensitive), so a user whose stored email casing differs from the attendee row will not be recognized as an attendee and may be wrongly forbidden. Likewise, duplicate prevention uses `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` (also case-sensitive), allowing the same mailbox to be added multiple times with different casing, which then persists via `attendees.createMany` and can lead to duplicate attendee rows and duplicate downstream calendar/email updates. The blacklist check is also inconsistent because `blacklistedGuestEmails` are lowercased but `guest` is not lowercased before `includes`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The booking lookup is `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } })` with no team/user scoping in the query itself, and the subsequent authorization widens access to any authenticated attendee of the booking. Any logged-in user who was once an attendee of any booking (including bookings belonging to a team they are not a member of) can permanently mutate that booking's attendee list, trigger calendar updates via the booking owner's credentials path, and cause emails to arbitrary addresses; the authorization is a post-fetch in-memory check rather than a scoped query, so future query changes (pagination, select reordering) can regress into a full IDOR, and attendees gain write access to resources owned by an organizer/team they have no other relationship with.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation fetches a booking purely by `id` (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } })`) and then grants write access if the caller is *any existing attendee* (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` followed by allowing the mutation when `isAttendee` is true). That means any authenticated user who is an attendee of a booking can add arbitrary new attendees to that booking, which then triggers `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (using the organizer/booking owner's credentials path) and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (emails to added addresses). This is an authorization/security defect exposed by the diff (attendees gaining permanent mutation capability over an organizer/team-owned booking).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts an unbounded array of guest emails with no .max() cap and no per-request rate limit, and each entry fans out into createMany rows plus one or more outbound emails. Any attendee or organizer can submit thousands of addresses in one mutation, creating thousands of attendee rows on a single booking and triggering mass email sends — an email-bombing/abuse vector against third-party mailboxes sent from the platform's mail domain (deliverability and reputation damage for the instance).

adjudication.rationale: The new mutation `addGuests` is exposed to any authorized user (organizer/attendee/team admin/owner) and accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` bound in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler writes all accepted emails via `attendees.createMany` and then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which fans out into multiple outbound emails (organizer + team members + per attendee) in `packages/emails/email-manager.ts`. The diff shows no server-side cap or throttling, so a single request can add thousands of rows and trigger mass email sends, constituting a concrete abuse/spam vector introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Email-sending failures are swallowed by `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, discarding the error object and reporting success to the caller. When guest-add emails fail (SMTP outage, template error), the organizer sees 'Guests added' success and never learns attendees were not notified, and operators debugging production have no stack trace or context because the error itself is not logged — the attendees exist in the DB but were never emailed, an unrecoverable silent divergence.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows the exception and discards `err` (no stack/metadata). The handler then still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` after having already mutated DB/calendar state, so a real failure (SMTP/template) would be silently ignored and not observable to the caller or operators from logs, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The write `prisma.booking.update({ where: { id: bookingId } })` re-derives authorization only from the earlier in-memory check with no ownership predicate in the update's where clause, and the guests are created before calendar/email work with no rollback path. Attendee rows are persisted even if eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees or email sending subsequently fails, leaving the booking's stored attendee list, the remote calendar event's attendee list, and the sent invitations permanently out of sync (added guests see the event in DB responses but were never invited or calendared).

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB write happens first (`prisma.booking.update({ where: { id: bookingId }, data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})`), then the handler performs side effects (`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`). There is no transaction/rollback or compensating delete if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (it is not caught), so attendee rows can be permanently persisted even though calendar invites/emails were not updated/sent, leaving DB vs. remote calendar/email out of sync exactly as described. (The authorization predicate-in-`where` point is weaker because an in-memory permission check exists, but the partial-failure inconsistency is directly verifiable from the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The admin/owner authorization check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so team admins who are not owners are denied even though the variable name and the check's intent (isTeamAdminOrOwner) is an OR. A team admin attempting to add guests to a team booking gets a FORBIDDEN error; only owners (or organizers/attendees) can use the feature, contradicting the permission model the code claims to implement.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed using `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`, meaning the user must be both an admin and an owner to pass that branch. This contradicts the variable name and the likely intended permission model (admin OR owner). As written, a team admin who is not also an owner will fail `isTeamAdminOrOwner` and can be blocked by the subsequent `FORBIDDEN` check unless they are also the organizer or an attendee.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The blacklist and existing-attendee dedup filters use exact string equality while blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased, so 'Spam@x.com' bypasses a blacklist entry 'spam@x.com', and a guest differing only in case from an existing attendee is not deduplicated. Blacklisted addresses receive event emails/ICS invites by simply varying case, and case-variant duplicates of existing attendees are inserted as new attendee rows, producing duplicate emails and duplicate calendar attendees.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` strings are not lowercased before checks: the filter uses `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. This makes both the blacklist check and existing-attendee dedup case-sensitive, allowing `Spam@x.com` to bypass a `spam@x.com` blacklist entry and allowing case-variant duplicates of existing attendee emails to be inserted via `attendees.createMany`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The server-side Zod schema validates only email format and does not enforce uniqueness (unlike the client-side copy in AddGuestsDialog), so duplicate guests in one request pass validation and are inserted twice by createMany. A crafted or retried request creates duplicate attendee rows for the same email; the server trusts a client-side refine that an API caller bypasses entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is only validated as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint, while the client dialog adds a uniqueness `refine`. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. Those duplicates are then passed to `attendees.createMany` (`guestsFullDetails`), which can insert duplicate attendee rows for the same email in a single request (or at least attempt to), since the server does not enforce uniqueness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] handleAdd sends the raw multiEmailValue array (which the UI initializes to [""] and keeps as an empty row when a user removes/leaves blanks) instead of validationResult.data, so any remaining empty string fails z.string().email() and blocks the whole submission. A user who adds two emails, fills one, and leaves the second row empty always sees the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error with no indication which row is the problem; the mutation never fires.

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, `multiEmailValue` is initialized/reset to `[""]` and `handleAdd` validates the entire array with `z.array(z.string().email())` (`safeParse(multiEmailValue)`). If the user leaves any row blank (e.g., adds a second email then leaves it empty), the array contains an empty string and validation fails, so the mutation is never called and the generic `emails_must_be_unique_valid` error is shown. The code also checks only `multiEmailValue.length === 0`, so `[""]` still proceeds to validation and fails. While the finding’s mention of not using `validationResult.data` is moot (it would equal the same array), the underlying blocked-submission behavior due to blank entries is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Email sending failures are swallowed with a bare console.log inside try/catch while the handler still returns success. The organizer sees 'Guests added' success toast and the DB rows are created, but no emails/ICS updates are sent and no error surfaces beyond a server log — silent partial failure with no user-visible signal and no error propagation for tests to assert.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and then continues to `return { message: "Guests added" }` (no error propagation). This means the client will treat the mutation as success and show the success toast (`onSuccess` in `AddGuestsDialog`) even if `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` fails. However, the finding overstates that "no ... ICS updates are sent": `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is awaited outside the `try/catch`, so calendar/ICS updates would still throw and fail the mutation if they error. The diff does verify silent email failure though.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The all-guests-filtered case throws BAD_REQUEST with the message 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' even when the actual cause was blacklisting or already-invited guests, conflating validation, dedup, and blacklist rejection into one client-facing error. Users adding an already-attendee or blacklisted email see a misleading 'Emails must be unique and valid' message; the client dialog likewise shows the invalid-email banner for what is a server-side dedup/blacklist rejection.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out already-attending emails and blacklisted emails, and if *all* inputs are filtered (`uniqueGuests.length === 0`) it throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`. This message maps to the locale string "Emails must be unique and valid", which is misleading when the real cause is "already an attendee" or "blacklisted" rather than invalid/duplicate formatting. The client (`AddGuestsDialog`) will surface this via `showToast(`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`...)`, so users see that conflated message. (However, the dialog’s red invalid-email banner is only set by client-side Zod validation and is not triggered by this server-side rejection.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] evt.attendees is built from the post-update attendee list (existing + new), so sendAddGuestsEmails sends the 'new guests added' variant only to pre-existing attendees, while brand-new guests receive the generic AttendeeScheduledEmail — check this is the intended per-audience split. If the intent was that newly added guests get an 'additional guests' notice, they instead get the standard scheduled-booking email; the branching in sendAddGuestsEmails (newGuests.includes) is the only thing distinguishing the two, and it depends on exact-case email matching.
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate describes that sendAddGuestsEmails iterates over the full (post-update) attendees list but uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` where `newGuests` is the input guests array, leading to the wrong audience receiving AttendeeAddGuestsEmail vs AttendeeScheduledEmail (and mentions email matching nuances). This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The add_members action is added unconditionally to every booking's actions array with no gating on booking status (cancelled/rejected bookings) or seat-based event types, unlike neighboring actions that carry conditions. Users can open the Add Guests dialog and mutate attendees on cancelled bookings or seated event types (where seatsPerTimeSlot capacity exists but is never checked in addGuestsHandler), overbooking seated events.

adjudication.rationale: The PR adds an unconditional "add_members" action in `BookingListItem` (no checks around booking state or event type) and the new `addGuestsHandler` mutates `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` without any guard on booking status (e.g., cancelled) or any capacity enforcement for seated events (`booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` is only copied onto the CalendarEvent `evt` but never validated before adding). This makes it possible to add attendees in cases that likely should be blocked and can overbook seated event types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so it is only true for users who are simultaneously admin AND owner, and the permission check falls through for plain admins or owners. A team admin (but not owner) or owner (but not admin) attempting to add guests to their team's booking is denied with FORBIDDEN even though the code clearly intends 'admin or owner' to be an authorized role; the condition is also evaluated twice with two separate awaits instead of one role query.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both admin AND owner. The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` will therefore reject a plain team admin or a plain team owner (who is neither organizer nor attendee) with `FORBIDDEN`, despite the variable name and typical authorization intent implying admin OR owner. This logic is introduced by the diff and is verifiably incorrect/overly restrictive. It also performs two separate awaited role checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Duplicate-guest detection compares the submitted email case-sensitively against booking.attendees and does not normalize case, while the blacklist comparison lowercases only the blacklist entries, not the guest email. Adding 'User@Example.com' when 'user@example.com' is already an attendee creates a duplicate Attendee row for the same person (duplicate DB rows and a duplicate attendee on the calendar event), and a guest email listed in BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS with different casing bypasses the blacklist and still gets booked and emailed.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, duplicate detection and blacklist checks are case-sensitive: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. The blacklist is lowercased (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but `guest` is not, so casing differences can bypass the blacklist. Similarly, an existing attendee `user@example.com` won’t block adding `User@Example.com`, potentially creating a duplicate attendee row and propagating to calendar/email logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The client-side Zod schema checks only uniqueness, not validity of individual entries before mutating, and MultiEmail always seeds state with an empty string that z.string().email() rejects on the server. A user who clicks Add while any chip is empty (the initial state is [""], and 'add another' pushes "") gets a server-side BAD_REQUEST surfaced as a raw error-code toast, and entries trimmed of whitespace client-side are never normalized before being persisted as attendee emails.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the client-side Zod schema is `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)`, which validates each entry as an email *and* enforces uniqueness—so it’s not “uniqueness only”. Also, the dialog seeds `multiEmailValue` with `[""]`, but `handleAdd()` runs `safeParse(multiEmailValue)` and, on failure, only sets `isInvalidEmail` without calling `addGuestsMutation.mutate(...)`, so clicking Add with empty chips does not trigger a server-side `BAD_REQUEST` toast. The diff does show the server can still reject duplicates against existing attendees/blacklist (since client doesn’t check that), but the finding’s core claims about client validation and empty-string submission causing server errors are not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The booking row is updated with createMany of attendees but the new attendee emails are never pushed to the existing calendar event attendees before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, and guests already present on the booking's calendar entry are not reconciled with the evt attendee list ordering. Depending on EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees semantics, the calendar event can be rebuilt with an attendee list that includes the just-created DB rows, so any failure between the Prisma update and the calendar update leaves the database and the external calendar event permanently out of sync (attendees on the booking but not invited on the calendar event), with no rollback of the created Attendee rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, and only afterwards `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called. There is no transaction/rollback or compensating logic if the calendar update throws/fails, so the booking can end up with new attendee rows in the database that were never applied to the external calendar. (The finding’s claim that new guests are “never pushed” to `evt.attendees` is incorrect—`evt.attendees` is built from `bookingAttendees.attendees`, which includes the newly created rows—but the out-of-sync/rollback issue is directly supported by the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The booking lookup has no ownership scoping in the where clause (only id: bookingId), deferring all authorization to the post-fetch role checks. Every fetch loads the full booking with attendees, references, and user credentials before authorization; correctness depends entirely on the (buggy) role check staying in sync, and any future caller that reuses this fetch pattern without the checks leaks other users' bookings.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, include: { attendees: true, eventType: true, destinationCalendar: true, references: true, user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true }}}})` before any authorization check. Authorization is only enforced after the full record (including sensitive `user.credentials`) is loaded. This also creates an information leak via differing errors (`NOT_FOUND` if missing vs `FORBIDDEN` if present but unauthorized), and correctness/security depend entirely on the post-fetch role checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Email send failures are swallowed with a bare console.log, so the success toast and 'Guests added' return value are reported even when no notifications or .ics updates went out. The organizer and guests silently never receive the updated invitation while the UI confirms success, and operators get no error signal beyond a console line.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and then continues to return `{ message: "Guests added" }`. That means the TRPC mutation will still resolve successfully and the UI (`AddGuestsDialog` onSuccess toast `t("guests_added")`) will report success even if notification emails (and their attached ICS payloads) fail to send, with no structured error/telemetry beyond a console line. However, the finding’s claim that “.ics updates went out” is not fully supported because calendar updates are performed separately via `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and would still fail the mutation if they throw.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New guests inherit the organizer's timeZone and locale rather than a neutral default. Guests who never booked themselves get calendar invitations and email renderings localized to the organizer's language and timezone, which is surprising for external guests in other locales.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, newly added guests are created with `timeZone: organizer.timeZone` and `locale: organizer.locale` (see `guestsFullDetails` mapping). Those values are then used to build `attendeesList` and the `CalendarEvent` sent to `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` and `sendAddGuestsEmails`, meaning the invite/email localization context for those guests is derived from the organizer, not the guest. This is a real, diff-grounded product/UX concern, but not an objectively verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The DB update commits before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs, and a calendar-update failure throws a raw 500 after the guests are already persisted, so retries are impossible. Guests are inserted into the booking, but if the calendar update fails the caller gets an error; on retry the dedup filter finds the guests already in booking.attendees, uniqueGuests.length === 0, and the user gets BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' instead of the calendar update being retried — the calendar is permanently out of sync with the booking and the operation reports failure for work that actually succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB write happens first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and only afterwards `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` is called with no error handling/transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will error after guests have already been persisted. On a retry, the handler re-fetches the booking, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already in `booking.attendees`, and then `if (uniqueGuests.length === 0) throw BAD_REQUEST "emails_must_be_unique_valid"`, preventing retrying the calendar sync and leaving calendar/booking potentially out of sync. This behavior is directly implied by the control flow in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Email send failure is swallowed with console.log (not even logging the error object) and the handler still returns { message: 'Guests added' }. If sendAddGuestsEmails rejects (e.g. one mail template render or SMTP send fails and Promise.all rejects), the mutation reports success, the UI toasts 'Guests added' and closes the dialog, while no one — organizer, existing attendees, or the new guests — received any email; the failure is invisible to the user and unobservable beyond a bare console.log with no err detail.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This makes email failures unobservable (no error object logged, no error propagated), but it does not necessarily make the mutation result incorrect because the core action (adding attendees via `prisma.booking.update(...createMany...)` and `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`) still succeeded. The finding is a valid review concern about error handling/observability for a new side effect, but not a verifiable functional defect given the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isTeamAdminOrOwner combines the two checks with && so only a team owner (who is both admin and owner) passes; team admins are denied. A team admin who manages the booking's event type but is not the owner is told 'you_do_not_have_permission' even though the intended gate (admin OR owner, matching the variable name and the permission model used elsewhere) would allow them; the permission check is stricter than the design intends, silently excluding admins.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which only evaluates to true for users who are both admin and owner. Given the variable name and the subsequent gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`, a team admin who is not also an owner would be denied permission to add guests, which is very likely unintended (admin OR owner is the expected check).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Blacklist filtering compares raw-case guest emails against a lowercased blacklist, so 'Spam@X.com' bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS while 'spam@x.com' is filtered. blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but the incoming guest string is not, so a mixed-case variant of a blacklisted address skips the filter: the guest is added to the booking and emailed, and because the dedup check (guest === attendee.email, also case-sensitive) stores the cased variant, the same address can be added again as 'other case' — the blacklist is silently bypassable and duplicate-variant emails accumulate.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but the filter checks `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without lowercasing `guest`, so mixed-case variants of a blacklisted email can bypass the blacklist. Similarly, deduping against existing attendees uses a case-sensitive equality (`guest === attendee.email`), and the server schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` does not enforce uniqueness/case normalization, allowing the same email to be added multiple times with different casing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When every submitted guest is filtered out (already an attendee or blacklisted), the error returned is 'emails_must_be_unique_valid', which misdescribes what went wrong. An organizer re-adding an existing attendee, or one whose guests are all blacklisted, sees 'Emails must be unique and valid' for perfectly valid, unique emails — the message points debugging in the wrong direction and the user has no way to learn the real cause (duplicate/blacklisted).

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, after filtering out emails that are already attendees or blacklisted (`uniqueGuests`), the code throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })` when `uniqueGuests.length === 0`. This can happen even when the submitted emails are syntactically valid and unique, but all were removed due to being existing attendees or blacklisted. The returned message therefore misdescribes the actual cause, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] findFirstOrThrow on the organizer with id coerced from booking.userId || 0 throws a raw Prisma error surfaced as a 500 when the booking has no user. For a booking with userId null (the || 0 sentinel), findFirstOrThrow rejects with a Prisma P2025 error that tRPC surfaces as an internal server error instead of a 4xx, and the client's t(err.message) toast renders a raw Prisma message.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null/undefined`, this coerces to `0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (Prisma not-found error) which is not converted into a `TRPCError`, so it will surface as an internal 500. The client’s `onError` uses `t(err.message)` and would therefore display a raw Prisma-derived message rather than a controlled i18n key. The use of the `|| 0` sentinel in the diff itself indicates this edge case is possible and unhandled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The guests array has no max length cap, so a single request can create an unbounded number of attendee rows and trigger an unbounded fan-out of emails and calendar updates. An authorized attendee can submit thousands of emails in one mutation: createMany inserts thousands of attendee rows, sendAddGuestsEmails fans out thousands of emails and N calendar operations — storage and outbound amplification with no count cap on a request path.

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (packages/trpc/.../addGuests.schema.ts) and the UI validation similarly only checks email format/uniqueness without a count cap (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx). The handler then `createMany` inserts all `uniqueGuests` into `booking.attendees` (packages/trpc/.../addGuests.handler.ts) and triggers expensive side effects: `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which maps over all attendees and sends an email per attendee (packages/emails/email-manager.ts). This makes the request path vulnerable to unbounded row creation and outbound email/calendar fan-out from a single authorized call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The organizer email subject uses this.calEvent.attendees[0].name, which is the first attendee rather than the booking counterpart, and crashes with a TypeError if attendees is empty. If the attendee list is ever empty the subject construction throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading name)' inside getNodeMailerPayload, which the handler's catch swallows into a bare console.log while the API still returns success — and when non-empty, the subject names an arbitrary guest instead of the person the email is about (existing OrganizerScheduledEmail usage passes the real attendee).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the email subject is built with `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`, which will throw if `this.calEvent.attendees` is empty (accessing `[0]` yields `undefined`). The diff also shows `addGuests.handler.ts` wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` in a `try/catch` that only `console.log`s and still returns success, so a runtime error here would be silently swallowed. Even when non-empty, using the first attendee for the organizer email subject can pick an arbitrary guest rather than the intended booking counterpart.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] isInvalidEmail is set on validation failure but never cleared on subsequent input or on success, so the stale error banner persists while the user fixes the emails. A user who triggers the validation error, corrects the emails, and submits successfully sees the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner still displayed underneath the (now valid) fields until they cancel and reopen the dialog — confusing feedback that misrepresents the current state.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when `ZAddGuestsInputSchema.safeParse(multiEmailValue)` fails, but it is never reset on subsequent `MultiEmail` edits or on mutation success. The only reset is in the Cancel button handler (`setIsInvalidEmail(false)`). On success, it closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`, but does not clear `isInvalidEmail`, so the error banner can remain visible after the user corrects inputs and/or when reopening the dialog.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] List items are keyed by array index while rows can be removed via splice, so React reuses DOM/state for the wrong email fields after a middle-row deletion. After removing an email from the middle of the list, the controlled values shift but React keys stay positional, producing misplaced focus/caret and transiently stale rendered values for the rows after the removed one — a classic index-key defect that bites the next edit of this component.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the email rows are rendered with `value.map((field, index) => (<li key={index}> ... ))`, and rows can be removed from the middle via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. This is the classic “index as key + deletions/reordering” problem: after deleting a middle row, React will reuse DOM/state for subsequent rows because their keys (indexes) shift, which can cause focus/caret jumps and transiently mismatched rendered values even though the controlled `value` array updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The event manager is built from ctx.user credentials while the booking/evt data is derived from the booking's organizer, so on behalf-of flows (attendee-triggered adds) the calendar update runs with the caller's credentials, not the organizer's. When an attendee (allowed by the permission check) adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees executes against the attendee's connected calendars, which hold no event for this booking — the calendar update is a silent no-op or fails, and the new guests never appear on the organizer's calendar event.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation allows attendees to add guests (`isAttendee` is permitted). But the calendar update uses an `EventManager` constructed from the caller (`...user` from `ctx.user`) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. Since `evt`/`booking` represent the organizer’s event, when an attendee triggers this flow the update will run using the attendee’s connected calendar credentials rather than the organizer’s, so it likely cannot find/update the organizer’s calendar event (silent no-op/failure), leaving guests not reflected on the organizer’s calendar.
